main_text.head: Ingens cacabus, Satana ignem vrgente despumans, & coelitus delapsis aquis iubinde repletus. XXXI.
main_text.p: EN Satan accensis hinc inde st torribus srgens, (ahenum sic tandem absumi spumantem hunc, sultus, Posse putat, lapsus complet quae coelitus humor. sic liceat nobis sanctorum effingere sortem, Quos Satanas, sariis hinc inde laborib9 instans, Exercet, frustra sefeque suosque fatigans. Ecquis enim tutus, nisi quos fidusq; potensque Tutatur coeli Christus qui confidet aroe ? Perge, Satan. Nam quo torres ardetius omnes Accendes, tanto mage despumaris ahenum, Puriur st tandem funde esca appareat imo.

page.notes: Woodcut: a cauldron on a fire with a devil pouring water from a jug into it, with clouds above. The first verse lines are set in italic. Several words are doubtful, notably "st", "srgens", "sultus", "aroe", "sariis", and "Puriur"; the line "Perge, Satan" may be misread. Running head and title are taken as printed; the final word "Crocodilus" is a catchword-like line at the foot right and may instead be a signature.
